screens.name: Home — default, omen available, omen unavailable, expanded policy
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–36 show the seated orb, daily-omen variants and enlarged layout, while filmstrips 74–78 show Home entering and leaving room destinations.
findings: Reduce decorative vertical space around the omen so its status and room destinations are easier to discover at 200% without competing with the orb.

screens.name: Approach — normal, enlarged, focused and pressed
screens.evidence: Sheets 3, 20, 22 and 30 show clear typing and speaking actions beneath a grounded orb, with distinct keyboard focus and pressed captures.
findings: Refine the table’s broad straight edge and surrounding contact shadows to make the title platform feel less like a separate overlay.

screens.name: Question composer — populated self and named-person variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–6 and 20 show populated self and Alex questions with context collapsed, a visible editor action and a dominant submission button.
findings: Tighten the gap between recipient, disclosure and question label so the centered form reads as one connected task.

screens.name: Question composer — expanded context and retrieved disclosure
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 and 31 show the expanded sharing disclosure occupying most of the enlarged viewport, with runtime evidence reporting complete retrieval and restored focus.
findings: Condense the centered disclosure into shorter labeled groups so the question remains easier to reach and distinguish from explanatory text.

screens.name: Question composer — constrained viewport and long question
screens.evidence: Sheets 31–32 show constrained populated questions with continuation cues, and supplied browser checks report retained drafts and reachable actions.
findings: Increase clearance between clipped text and the continuation badges so partially visible lines do not visually merge with scrolling controls.

screens.name: Named-person selection — empty, populated and corrected
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6, 21–22 and 32 show selected Someone, empty-name guidance, disabled commitment and a valid Alex draft.
findings: Use a consistent selection-marker position for Myself/Someone and the other choice families.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — steps 1, 2 and 3, unselected
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–13 show all three prompts, progress, radio choices, custom-answer access and disabled continuation at both text scales.
findings: Give the parchment choices more restrained edge shading to preserve their material identity without making every row look identically stamped.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — selected, focused, pressed and one-question variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 14, 19–21 and 29–30 show radio selection, enabled Reveal/Continue, strong focus outlines and separate press captures.
findings: Keep focus, selection and press treatments visually distinct while simplifying the multiple nested outlines.

screens.name: Custom follow-up answer — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 show an empty writing area, explicit minimum-entry guidance and disabled Continue at normal and enlarged text.
findings: Reduce the oversized prompt’s vertical footprint at 200% so writing receives more immediate emphasis.

screens.name: Custom follow-up answer — populated and constrained
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–31 show short and long custom answers with enabled Reveal and visible continuation controls in constrained views.
findings: Leave a clearer blank inset above and below the visible writing to separate clipped text from continuation cues.

screens.name: Expanded editors — question and custom answer, full and constrained height
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show both editors with counters and Done/Cancel, supported by 24 reported browser cases covering draft preservation and focus return.
findings: Add more internal text-edge clearance so enlarged first and last visible lines do not crowd the paper cut and scroll badges.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheet 37 shows a concise age question, birthday-free explanation and two clear responses at both scales.
findings: Keep the concise composition while slightly strengthening separation between the two responses and the detailed shelf painting.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheet 38 shows labeled day/month/year fields, optionality, Skip and responsive two-row enlargement.
findings: Give the three writing fields a more consistent inset edge so they read as one birthday group.

screens.name: Age restriction — onboarding and edited-birthday blocked states
screens.evidence: Sheets 1 and 38–39 show an explicit age restriction and a correction action that remains visible at 200%.
findings: Shorten the enlarged heading’s vertical footprint while retaining the direct restriction and correction explanation.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40 show the corrected-birthday task, retained age requirement and Check birthday, with the enlarged back action continuing below the capture.
findings: Compress the explanatory group to bring the return action closer to the birthday form at 200%.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected, skipped route and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 40–41 show optional themes, a selected checkmark and the primary label changing from Skip focus to Continue.
findings: Reserve a consistent marker column so selected and unselected centered theme labels keep the same visual position.

screens.name: Birthday editing — populated, partial and invalid
screens.evidence: Sheets 1–2 and 72 show saved values, field-specific missing-day feedback, invalid-date feedback and Save/Cancel/Remove actions.
findings: Keep validation adjacent to the field group while reducing its enlarged vertical spacing so recovery controls stay closer together.

screens.name: Birth time — initial, invalid and forgotten
screens.evidence: Sheets 8–9 and 71 show optional time entry, a precise accepted range, an unknown-time route and confirmation that birthday is retained after forgetting details.
findings: Condense the centered time-format example to reduce repetition around the already explicit 24-hour label.

screens.name: Birth city — empty and retained draft
screens.evidence: Sheets 6–7 and 70–71 show empty and Copenhagen drafts, disabled/enabled search, optional Skip and provider disclosure.
findings: Group search guidance and optional Skip more tightly so the city-entry task remains the clear center of the screen.

screens.name: Birth city — service failure and no results
screens.evidence: Sheets 7–8 distinguish unavailable service from no matches and explain retained saved details, with supplied evidence reporting live recovery.
findings: Shorten the enlarged saved-chart explanation so the distinct error and its recovery action appear sooner.

screens.name: Birth city — live search results
screens.evidence: Sheets 9–10 show Copenhagen matches differentiated by region and country, including enlarged wrapping.
findings: Use a slightly stronger typographic distinction between city name and geographic qualifier to speed centered-list scanning.

screens.name: Birth profile — saved and recovered result
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 group the Moon/rising result, location, time and saved-on-device status above Done, Edit and Forget.
findings: Keep the result grouping while reducing the parchment’s uniform rectangular appearance with subtler, more local contact shading.

screens.name: Planning and research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 50–51 show distinct phase descriptions, waiting expectations, cancellation and no-charge reassurance at both text scales.
findings: Make the phase wording slightly more concrete so Finding the thread and Reading the signs communicate meaningful progress beyond atmosphere.

screens.name: Planning failure and prediction failure
screens.evidence: Sheets 25–26 show retry, editing, prediction-stage answer review and explicit no-charge feedback.
findings: Preserve the strong recovery hierarchy while tightening spacing between secondary recovery routes.

screens.name: Sensitive-question redirects — planning and prediction
screens.evidence: Sheets 56–57 show a prominent external support action, alternative-question routes and a statement that no reading or memory was added.
findings: Place the short explanation immediately before the support action so the reason for leaving the prediction flow is established first.

screens.name: Voice unavailable
screens.evidence: Sheets 36–37 show an explicit voice failure, microphone guidance, a dominant typing fallback and retry.
findings: Keep the typing fallback dominant and reduce decorative orb space where it delays the recovery message.

screens.name: Opening — normal and golden, early and settled states
screens.evidence: Sheets 41–45 and filmstrip 79 show a stationary opening orb, skip affordance and rising result slip, with a conspicuous dark circular surround in golden settled captures.
findings: Blend the golden surround into the room’s light rather than leaving a visible circular backing behind the painted orb.

screens.name: Reveal — normal, enlarged and expanded actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 52–54 show the full forecast, uncertainty, date, Why/Share and expanded reminder/plan/edit actions, with enlarged actions extending below the first viewport.
findings: Reduce nonessential vertical spacing at 200% so the forecast’s follow-up actions require less scrolling without shrinking its text.

screens.name: Reading details — all disclosures collapsed
screens.evidence: Sheets 52–53 show four consistently labeled disclosure rows and a direct return to the forecast.
findings: Use a quieter wood treatment for disclosure rows so four equal boards do not compete as primary actions.

screens.name: Reading details — explanation expanded and standalone Why
screens.evidence: Sheets 28 and 54 show Recorded context, Scenario assumption and Limits separated into centered parchment passages.
findings: Shorten the visual reading measure and strengthen section spacing to make long centered explanations easier to resume after scrolling.

screens.name: Reading details — saved answers expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–27 show question headings and complete multi-paragraph answers, with enlarged content continuing beyond the viewport.
findings: Make each question-and-answer group more visually bounded so users can relocate a specific answer within the centered text.

screens.name: Reading details — assumptions expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 27–28 show an explicit condition inside parchment with a close action and the next disclosure beneath it.
findings: Reduce oversized heading space at 200% to bring more of the condition into the initial view.

screens.name: Reading details — background sources expanded
screens.evidence: Sheet 29 distinguishes background-only sources, italic publisher captions, source text, dates and external links.
findings: Strengthen the centered separation of publisher, source text and external-link action so long citations are easier to scan.

screens.name: Dense reading stress states — answers, explanation and sources
screens.evidence: Sheets 23–24 show near-continuous enlarged centered text on very tall parchment, with supplied checks reporting complete text and successful end-of-sheet traversal.
findings: Introduce stronger passage landmarks and more frequent visual grouping so dense retained text does not become an undifferentiated vertical column.

screens.name: Check-in — no outcome selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 15–17 and 45–46 keep the forecast above three outcomes with explicit selection guidance and disabled Save.
findings: Tighten the enlarged forecast-to-outcome spacing so the check-in decision receives more of the first viewport.

screens.name: Check-in — selected but unsaved
screens.evidence: Sheet 17 shows a selected radio, Not saved yet and enabled Save, with runtime evidence distinguishing unsaved drafts from persistence.
findings: Keep the unsaved status close to Save while reducing the tall enlarged card’s internal gaps.

screens.name: Check-in — saved Yes, Not quite and Not yet
screens.evidence: Sheets 16 and 46–48 show all saved outcomes with Change outcome and unchanged check-in dates, supported by reported reload checks.
findings: Visually distinguish the saved outcome from forecast metadata a little more strongly inside the centered card.

screens.name: Check-in — original question expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 15 and 45–46 show the original question as a separate disclosure beneath the exact forecast, including focused enlarged variants.
findings: Reduce disclosure spacing so the expanded original question does not push all subsequent actions unnecessarily far down.

screens.name: Check-in — editing saved outcome, cancelled and changed
screens.evidence: Sheets 55–56 show editing, Cancel, restored saved Yes and changed saved Not quite, with reported focus restoration and persistence.
findings: Keep Cancel visually close to Save at enlarged text so the reversible editing state is immediately apparent.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–34 and filmstrip 78 show a bottle seated on a shelf, an empty-state heading and Ask the Ball.
findings: Add a short explicit no-saved-readings statement so the poetic empty-state heading does not carry the whole explanation.

screens.name: History — populated, multiple rows and persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheets 32–34 show shelf-supported forecast cards, dates, suggested check-ins and a persisted Yes outcome.
findings: Add a subtle opening affordance to each history card so it is clearly a route into the saved reading.

screens.name: Sky — sample stars, selected theme and question
screens.evidence: Sheet 69 shows an offline sample notice, framed night-window selector and selected-question parchment, with the enlarged selector continuing below the viewport.
findings: Compact the header and offline notice so the enlarged theme selector and resulting question remain more closely connected.

screens.name: Circles — offline and failed retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 18–19 and filmstrip 75 show distinct initial/retried offline messages, a primary retry and a private-questions explanation.
findings: Reduce the large heading’s vertical footprint so the privacy explanation is less deeply displaced at 200%.

screens.name: You — populated profile, plan and memory
screens.evidence: Sheets 72–73 show birthday/profile information on parchment followed by plan and editable memory, with lower content continuing behind the viewport boundary.
findings: Create clearer centered section separation between profile, plan and memory so the page is easier to navigate at enlarged text.

screens.name: You — empty memory and settings controls
screens.evidence: Sheets 22–23 and 58 show empty-memory copy, display/sound switches, focused Reduce motion and distinct on/off positions.
findings: Give the settings groups more consistent vertical separation so subscription, display and saved-data actions are easier to distinguish.

screens.name: Plans — weekly and monthly selection, enlarged and scrolled
screens.evidence: Sheets 49–50 and filmstrip 74 show all three prices, selected plans, renewal language, simulation labeling and packs, with keyboard checks reported for every option.
findings: Reduce the ledger’s unused space and group the selected price, renewal terms and commitment action more tightly at 200%.

screens.name: Share — preview and expanded invitation/reminder options
screens.evidence: Sheets 65–66 and 68 show preview, Enlarge, Download, image-text access, replay and privacy wording, with additional options expanded below.
findings: Shorten the vertical path from preview to privacy guidance so users review what is shared before reaching secondary sharing routes.

screens.name: Share — enlarged image inspection and story view
screens.evidence: Sheets 61–62 and 69–70 show a larger complete share artifact, direct image-text access and a return-to-sharing action.
findings: Reduce oversized heading space at 200% so more of the artifact is visible before scrolling.

screens.name: Share — readable image text
screens.evidence: Sheets 67–68 present the forecast, uncertainty, brand and check-in date as scalable text above Download and the image.
findings: Keep the accessible text primary and reduce the duplicate image’s visual weight beneath it.

screens.name: Share export — preparing, download started and failed/retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 60–61 distinguish preparation, background continuation, download started and recoverable failure, supported by reported real PNG export and retry checks.
findings: Present the short export status in a more compact scene grouping so the vast empty cabinet does not separate feedback from its exit action.

screens.name: Invitation — copied result and cancelled sharing
screens.evidence: Sheets 62–65 show cancellation, successful copy and repeated sharing across three widths, with View link near the enlarged footer boundary.
findings: Increase the content’s bottom clearance and expose its continuation more clearly where View link meets the fixed Done region.

screens.name: Invitation — clipboard-denied fallback and visible URL
screens.evidence: Sheets 58–59 show the labeled selectable URL and fallback explanation, but the enlarged encoded link is fragmented across lines and fades at the field edge.
findings: Strengthen the whole-link selection affordance and continuation indicator so copying does not depend on interpreting the fragmented encoded URL.

screens.name: Reminder — unsupported browser notice
screens.evidence: Sheets 66–67 explicitly state that no browser reminder was scheduled and provide the check-back date and native-app boundary.
findings: Separate the check-back date into a short centered line to make the useful fallback easier to retain.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home, Approach and opening captures show painted reflections, a substantial brass stand and table contact, with supplied stationary-bounds and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Remove the visibly bounded dark surround in golden reveal states so illumination feels continuous with the room.

components.name: Room destination controls
components.evidence: Filmstrips 74–78 show small illustrated History, Circles and Plans destinations, but no dedicated destination focus or press captures are supplied.
findings: Make the small centered captions more prominent and provide direct browser focus/press evidence for these destination controls.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Home, Sky, History and You captures consistently show five labeled destinations with a gold active marker and central orb.
findings: Keep scrolling content visibly clear of the decorative top edge so cropped card text is not mistaken for obscured content.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Home uses a storybook wordmark while flow headers show balances or explicitly labeled test status at both scales.
findings: Standardize the header’s vertical spacing across room and modal views to reduce perceived composition jumps.

components.name: Primary wood button
components.evidence: Sheets 20–22 and 30 show enabled, disabled, focused and pressed wood controls, supported by keyboard and focus-pixel evidence.
findings: Vary local contact shading more naturally and reduce the repeated stretched-board appearance on very tall buttons.

components.name: Secondary text action
components.evidence: Across forms and reading screens, gold text actions share styling with some gold informational labels.
findings: Use consistent spacing and a restrained non-color action cue where secondary links could be confused with informational labels.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Sheets 11–14 and 21 show readable parchment choices with empty/selected radios and distinct keyboard-focus states.
findings: Simplify the layered focus border while retaining its strong contrast against both parchment and room.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Composer captures show plain writing paper, a persistent label and strong ink, with reported minimum populated-field contrast of 10.706:1.
findings: Make the paper’s inset depth more consistent with adjacent parchment without introducing texture beneath the writing.

components.name: Large-text and long-content input
components.evidence: Sheets 24–25 and 31 show enlarged writing, scroll tracks, edge fades and continuation badges with several partially clipped visible lines.
findings: Increase interior edge padding and badge separation so scrolling text remains visually distinct from the field boundary.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheets 22–23 and 58 show inset switches with different knob positions and focus outlines, supported by keyboard, persistence and contrast checks.
findings: Strengthen the on/off track distinction slightly to make state recognition faster without relying on knob position alone.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 34–36 show available content, exhausted attempt, unavailable result and expanded policy inside parchment.
findings: Keep result, attempt status and policy visually separate so the policy does not dominate the enlarged omen.

components.name: Sky stars and selected-question surface
components.evidence: Sheet 69 shows a wood-framed night window, spatial star labels, selected Love and a separate question card.
findings: Bring the selected theme and resulting question into a tighter visual group, especially after the enlarged selector changes to a text grid.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheets 18–19 place retry and privacy parchment against the hearth painting with distinct initial and repeated failure copy.
findings: Reduce oversized enlarged headings so the informational parchment remains part of the immediate recovery context.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 32–34 show bottles, supporting shelves and cards carrying forecast, date and outcome/check-in status.
findings: Add a subtle consistent cue that the whole centered card opens a saved reading.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 49–50 show visible price and interval for each plan with a checkmark, backed by reported complete radio-keyboard tests.
findings: Reduce excess space between ledger entries and strengthen the selected entry’s grouping with its renewal terms.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sheets 61–62 and 65–70 show a coherent vertical artifact with a dark headline backing, uncertainty text, date, Enlarge and accessible text alternatives.
findings: Increase headline prominence within the small preview so its content is more recognizable before enlargement.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Error, voice, birth-search, export and unsupported-reminder states name the problem and offer a relevant next step.
findings: Use a more compact grouping of message and action on short notices to avoid separating them across an otherwise empty cabinet.

components.name: Typography system
components.evidence: The sheets consistently use storybook display lettering and centered serif body text, but dense enlarged explanations form long visually uniform columns.
findings: Retain centered alignment while improving paragraph landmarks, line length and the relative size of long display headings.

components.name: Atmospheric background and camera continuity
components.evidence: Filmstrips 74–78 show connected cabinet/hearth/shelf paintings and focus changes, but destination content arrives while the background continues reframing across later samples.
findings: Coordinate the room reframing and interface arrival so the destination feels physically reached before its content settles.

components.name: Parchment information card
components.evidence: Information cards show cut edges, warm falloff and contact shadows, although tall sheets retain a largely uniform rectangular face.
findings: Refine local edge thickness and contact shadow rather than adding more texture to give long sheets believable material depth.

components.name: Birthday input
components.evidence: Sheets 1–2, 38–40 and 72 show persistent labels, enlarged reflow and field-specific invalid/partial states.
findings: Unify the inset paper edges across all three fields to strengthen their grouping as one date.

components.name: Age confirmation control
components.evidence: Sheet 37 presents direct over/under-13 responses and corresponding restriction/correction states appear in sheets 38–40.
findings: Keep the two responses clearly separated from decorative shelf lines at both scales.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 40–41 show four themes, optional Skip, a selected check and an updated Continue action.
findings: Use a reserved marker area so selection does not disturb the centered label’s visual balance.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheets 10–11 and 72–73 consolidate signs and saved birth details with clear editing actions.
findings: Distinguish editable actions from profile facts using consistent spacing and action cues inside the centered surface.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Sheets 6–11 and 70–71 cover optional entry, invalid time, retained draft, search failures/results and saved/forgotten outcomes.
findings: Shorten repeated helper text and keep each recovery explanation tightly attached to the relevant field.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Sheets 5–6, 21–22 and 32 show recipient selection, a labeled name field and empty/valid commitment states.
findings: Match the recipient selection marker’s placement and weight to the other choice controls.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Sheets 26–29 and 52–54 show consistent chevrons and expanded content, supported by reported ordered-text and keyboard traversal checks.
findings: Quiet the wood styling and strengthen the opened section’s content grouping so disclosure navigation does not dominate the explanation.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Sheets 60–61 distinguish preparation, download initiation and failure, with reported duplicate prevention, actual PNG retry and focus restoration.
findings: Bring status and available action closer together while preserving the precise Download started wording.

components.name: Close and Back controls
components.evidence: Sheets 19–20 show visible keyboard outlines around Close and Back, and supplied measurements establish at least 44×44 targets.
findings: Standardize their header position across modal families to make exit and return locations more predictable.

components.name: Outcome selector and saved status
components.evidence: Sheets 15–17 and 45–56 distinguish no selection, unsaved choice, saved outcomes and reversible corrections at both scales.
findings: Give saved outcome text slightly stronger visual emphasis than adjacent forecast metadata.

components.name: Modal and notice container
components.evidence: Sharing notices use a fixed Done region while reading overlays use header exits, with some enlarged content meeting a hard lower clipping boundary.
findings: Provide a more explicit scroll continuation and consistent bottom clearance above fixed modal actions.

components.name: Invitation-link field
components.evidence: Sheets 58–59 show a dashed selectable URL inset with wrapping and fade, supported by reported whole-link selection and successful fresh-profile decoding.
findings: Make Select entire link a clearer interaction cue and strengthen overflow indication at 200%.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser evaluations; supplied runtime results were considered as reported evidence and were not independently rerun.
Corresponding normal, enlarged and transition captures are grouped above; scores assess the represented states rather than treating every screenshot filename as a separate screen.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native keyboard, tilt, haptics, OS sharing and native performance remain deferred without blanket browser-score deductions.
Connected Circles functionality and real billing are not demonstrated; offline recovery and explicitly simulated plans are the evaluated states.
Fixture readings, synthetic sources and layout stress text establish interface coverage, not predictive accuracy or production model quality.
Chronological still filmstrips establish sampled visual continuity, not continuous-video observation or frame rate; performance claims rely on the separately supplied timing results.
Below-viewport content is not assumed unreachable: reported scrolling and layout checks support access, while visible clipping, density and weak continuation remain browser presentation concerns.
No hard-gate failure is established by the supplied evidence, but the authorized A≥9 and F≥9 threshold is not met across every screen and component.
Dimension scores support the specified A, F and weighted-overall calculations; null is used only where a dimension is genuinely inapplicable.
topFixes: Improve room-transition choreography: synchronize destination content with background reframing and remove the golden orb’s visible circular backing.
Refine material depth through local contact shadows and edge thickness; repeated wood boards and tall parchment still look too uniformly layered.
Improve long centered reading with clearer passage landmarks, restrained heading sizes and stronger grouping without changing alignment.
Give enlarged inputs and invitation URLs clearer interior margins and continuation cues, and preserve obvious clearance above fixed modal actions.
Reduce decorative vertical spacing on enlarged context, plans, Sky and check-in views so related decisions and actions remain closer together.
Clarify small room-destination and history-card affordances and supply direct browser focus/press evidence for room destinations.
